prompt:
A student burns $0.30\ \text{g}$ of ethanol under a copper can holding $50.0\ \text{cm}^3$ of water. The water temperature rises by $12.0\ °\text{C}$.

**(a)** State why the mass of the water can be taken as $50.0\ \text{g}$. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the heat absorbed by the water, in kJ. ($c = 4.18\ \text{J g}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}$) **[1]**

**(c)** Suggest one reason why the enthalpy of combustion calculated from this experiment is less exothermic than the literature value. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** The density of water is (about) $1.00\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$ ✓

**(b)** $q = mc\Delta T = 50.0 \times 4.18 \times 12.0 = 2508\ \text{J} \approx 2.51\ \text{kJ}$ ✓

**(c)** Heat lost to the surroundings / heat absorbed by the can / incomplete combustion of ethanol ✓
